title: Pathways HealthTech — Console Usage Atlas & Cost Breakdown Demo
next_steps: Share Route-level pricing spreadsheet and example billing export
Send SOC2 and VPC/private deployment whitepaper
Provision trial console account for Pathways (2-week) and seed with sample routes
action_items: Jordan: Send pricing spreadsheet and sample invoice (due 2026-07-10)
Priya: Set up trial console account and import sample routes (due 2026-07-13)
Marta: Provide representative traffic profile and top 10 prompt templates (due 2026-07-12)
Samir/Finance: Confirm budget and legal timeline (due 2026-07-17)
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Pathways HealthTech through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. Customer is evaluating host vs dedicated vs private deployment for production; key concerns are per-route cost visibility, token-level attribution for multi-tenant service, and SOC2 / VPC compliance. Agreed to a 2-week trial and a pilot kick-off next week.
topics: Batching and KV cache impact on unit economics
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, just to confirm audio — can you hear me?
[00:04] Evan: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:06] Jordan: Awesome. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Liam on CS. We'll walk through the Console usage atlas and how you can see route-level costs.
[00:14] Priya: Hi all — quick agenda: 1) Console tour focusing on per-route dashboards; 2) cost breakdown and token attribution; 3) a short discussion on deployment options and security; 4) next steps.
[00:24] Marta: Sounds good. We're primarily interested in how we can tie model call costs back to our product features and teams.
[00:29] Priya: Great, that's exactly what the route dashboards are built for. I'll share my screen — bear with me, sometimes the screen share lags.
[00:37] [00:38] Priya: Okay pulling up the Console home. Top left you can see usage lens — we surface routes as first-class entities. Here's a fictitious multi-tenant app with routes: "clinical-summary", "billing-assist", "patient-chat".
[00:52] Priya: For each route we show throughput, p95 latency, tokens in/out, and an estimated ru - ah, cost-per-token breakdown. The cost is inferred from your routing and model choices and the quantization profile.
[01:10] Evan: Quick question — does that cost reflect caching and batching benefits? Our traffic is bursty and we rely on prefix caching for repeated patient prompts.
[01:18] Priya: Yes, we model automatic prefix/KV caching and batching. In the route view there's a toggle to simulate different batching sizes or to include cache-hit rates. See this slider here — if you increase cache hit rate from 10% to 40% it drops your token unit cost significantly.
[01:33] [01:35] Jordan: To be explicit — the Console uses observed runtime telemetry, so the cost number is grounded in real traces, not just a static per-token price. It's useful for forecasting and chargebacks.
[01:44] Marta: Nice. Can we map routes to teams for billing? We have multiple product teams sharing the same model endpoint.
[01:49] Priya: Yep — under 'Route Tags' you can assign tags like team:clinical, product:billing. The billing export then aggregates by tags. We'll show an example export shortly.
[01:58] [02:00] Priya: Now switching to the per-route timeline. You'll see spikes corresponding to batch sizes and the KV cache utilization graph below. Notice the purple line is average token-per-request; the orange is p95 latency.
[02:13] Evan: That p95 seems a bit higher than our internal targets — how much of that is model selection vs hardware?
[02:19] Priya: Good question. We annotate each trace with model variant and hardware tier — e.g., gptx-llama-quant on A100 vs the faster 80GB Ampere or H100 variants. There's an attribution panel showing percent latency by model/hardware.
[02:33] [02:35] Samir: For us, compliance is non-negotiable. If we go private or VPC, are the same Console metrics available in the private deployment? We need near identical observability.
[02:44] Jordan: Yes, that's a core promise. Private deployments include the same control plane integration; you get local telemetry forwarded to the Console control plane or retained on-prem depending on your policy. We also have an on-prem agent for audit logs.
[02:58] Priya: And the audit trail includes per-token traces with request IDs — redaction optional. You can integrate with your KMS so we never retain plaintext inputs in our control plane.
[03:09] Anya: On the finance side — how do you present costs on invoices? We need to reconcile with our internal chargeback model.
[03:15] Jordan: The billing export maps tokens to route tags and model variants. So you can get a CSV with columns: timestamp, route, team_tag, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate. We can also output a sample report matching your accounting format.
[03:30] [03:32] Priya: I'll jump into the 'Cost Explorer' tab — here you can pivot by route, by model, or by customer-id. The route cost waterfall shows how much of the spend is base model compute, caching savings, and batching gains.
[03:45] Marta: Do you show the delta for quantized vs fp16? We run some models quantized to int8 and see different memory/latency tradeoffs.
[03:52] Priya: We do. For each model variant we attach a 'quality vs cost' panel that approximates perplexity or a proxy metric from your eval set if you upload one. So you can compare int8-quantized throughput and cost to fp16 baseline.
[04:07] Evan: How accurate are those quality proxies? We need to ensure production output doesn't regress.
[04:12] Priya: It's a proxy — not a replacement for your eval suite. We recommend using Redwood Optimize to run prompt-level eval regressions; the Console will ingest those results and flag regressions per-route.
[04:23] [04:25] Jordan: Quick note on routing policies: you can set fallbacks per route. If dedicated capacity is saturated we can fallback to hosted low-latency variants or to cheaper batch-optimized nodes based on a policy you define.
[04:38] Samir: That fallback behavior — is it automatic? Can we set SLOs?
[04:41] Priya: Yes — SLO policies are first-class. You set p95 and cost budget thresholds. If latency budgets are violated, routing shifts to the high-priority pool; if cost budget is hit, you can opt for fallback to a lower-cost model variant.
[04:56] [05:00] Priya: I'm going to demo an example — "billing-assist" route has 1M calls/day. Right now it's pinned to a 16-GPU dedicated pool. See the per-route cost curve here: the majority of cost comes from long-context summaries, high token-out.
[05:16] Priya: If we change the model variant to a 4-bit quantized family and enable prefix caching with 35% hit rate, estimated cost drops ~28% with negligible impact on our eval proxy.
[05:30] [05:32] Marta: Hold on — what's the QA process for quantized models? We can't just ship a quantized model without regression testing.
[05:37] Priya: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize can run your evaluation bench across versions and create a regression alert tied to a prompt set. Console surfaces those alerts per route and can block rollouts automatically if you enable safety gates.
[05:48] Evan: Could you show the billing export?
[05:50] Priya: Sure exporting now — sample CSV link: https://redwood.ai/samples/pathways-billing.csv (note: sample). The CSV contains route-level token counts, model variants, and cost columns. You can plug it into your ledger.
[06:05] [06:08] Anya: That helps. We also need a breakdown by environment (staging vs prod) and by customer tenant — can you tag at the request level?
[06:16] Jordan: Yes, you can pass metadata with each request and Redwood will index it. We recommend a combination of route tags plus metadata like tenant_id so you have both feature-level and tenant-level chargebacks.
[06:29] [06:30] Priya: Switching gears — security. We support SSO via SAML/Okta; RBAC at route and team level; data retention policies and optional request data redaction. For private deployments you can configure the control plane to not transmit user inputs off your VPC.
[06:46] Samir: KMS integration? We use an HSM-backed KMS and need envelope encryption at rest.
[06:52] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS— envelope encryption supported, keys never leave your KMS, HSM is supported for on-prem. We'll include the KMS setup doc in the follow-ups.
[07:02] [07:05] Evan: For the pilot we want to run a week of A/B testing: our current hosted endpoint vs Redwood dedicated with 4-bit quantized variant. Can Redwood handle traffic mirroring?
[07:14] Priya: Yes, traffic mirroring is supported. You can mirror a percentage of production traffic to a pilot route; Console will show side-by-side metrics and per-request diffs. We also provide a sample harness for deterministic comparisons.
[07:28] Marta: About latency — our SLA is 200ms p95 for patient-chat. Can Redwood meet that on dedicated?
[07:34] Priya: On appropriately sized dedicated pools with batching disabled (or small batches) and using H100-class hardware, we've consistently hit <200ms p95 for short-context chat. For long context tasks you should expect higher latency. We'll run benchmarks with your prompts.
[07:50] [07:55] Jordan: Quick pause — any low-hanging compliance items?
[07:58] Samir: SOC2 and audit logs are required. We also need a data processing agreement and specifics on data residency (we have EU-only PHI).
[08:07] Jordan: Understood. We'll share our SOC2 report and the DPA template. For EU PHI we'd recommend private VPC with regional isolation — we have EU regions and on-prem options.
[08:20] [08:23] Priya: Back to the Console — here's a 'What-if' cost simulator where you can set expected traffic and see projected monthly spend. It factors in model selection, expected cache hit rate, batching strategy, and dedicated pool pricing.
[08:36] Anya: Can you annotate invoices with internal GL codes?
[08:39] Jordan: We can include metadata in the billing export so you can map to GL codes. We can also generate custom invoice templates for enterprise deals.
[08:48] [08:50] Priya: I'm going to drill into a single request trace — you'll see the request id, token breakdown between prompt and completion, which model shards were used, and the cache hit flag. Note there's sometimes small transcription artifacts in our demo traces — ignore the gibberish.
[09:05] Marta: The trace shows a 25% cache hit for a clinical-summary route; if we improve that to 60% what's realistic?
[09:12] Priya: Depends on prompt templating and reuse. With structured prompts and an upstream caching layer you can see up to 60-70% for certain workflows. The Console's heatmap helps you spot high-repeat prefixes.
[09:26] [09:30] Evan: In terms of pricing model — how do you price Dedicated? Is it an absolute monthly commit or can we do burst capacity?
[09:37] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with a commit. We have flexible burst credit options for traffic spikes and autoscaling policies. Commit size determines base unit cost and SLAs. We can tailor the reserved pool size for Pathways.
[09:49] Samir: If we start with hosted and then move to dedicated, how disruptive is that?
[09:54] Priya: Minimal from an API perspective — same endpoints, same route configs. The Console route config points to a policy that selects hosted vs dedicated. Rollouts are controlled in the Console with canary options.
[10:08] [10:10] Jordan: We'll do a quick Q&A — any blockers?
[10:12] Anya: Budget approval timeline — we need costs broken down by month and by feature.
[10:17] Jordan: We'll send a route-level pricing spreadsheet.
[10:19] [10:20] Priya: One more demo — Optimize suggestions: the Console will surface quantization suggestions and batching recommendations with estimated savings and risk score. For example, it recommended lowering max_tokens on 'clinical-summary' to reduce token-out waste.
[10:36] Marta: How does Redwood compute the risk score? Is it based on your evals?
[10:40] Priya: It's a heuristic combining model drift from your eval set, customer-provided quality constraints, and historical rollout outcomes. It suggests either safe, moderate, or risky.
[10:51] Evan: Let's talk pilot scope — what do you need from our side?
[10:55] Jordan: 1) Representative prompt corpus and traffic traces; 2) a list of top 10 routes and their owners; 3) access to a staging region or allow us to mirror traffic; 4) confirmation on whether this will be EU-only.
[11:09] [11:12] Marta: We'll get the prompt corpus and a traffic sample.
[11:15] Samir: Legal needs a vendor security questionnaire — can you fill ours out?
[11:18] Jordan: Yes — we'll start that after sending the SOC2 and DPA.
[11:22] [11:25] Priya: Demo note — sometimes the Console shows slightly different token counts due to tokenization differences between tokenizers; we try to normalize but expect small deltas.
[11:36] Anya: That's fine as long as we can reconcile consistently.
[11:40] Evan: Any limitations around multi-tenant isolation?
[11:43] Priya: You can enforce tenant isolation with per-tenant route pinning to dedicated pools, or use request-level metadata to apply rate limits and quotas. For strict isolation, private deployment is recommended.
[11:56] [12:00] Jordan: I'm going to recap decisions and next steps.
[12:03] Jordan: Pathways wants a 2-week trial of the Console, seeded with your routes; the pilot will include an A/B mirror comparing hosted vs dedicated quantized variant; Redwood to send pricing sheet and security docs.
[12:16] Marta: Confirmed. We'll also provide the prompt corpus and traffic traces.
[12:20] Samir: We'll review budget and legal timeline.
[12:23] Jordan: Great. Priya, anything to add?
[12:25] Priya: I'll provision the trial account and import the sample routes. I'll also set up a demo dashboard with the requested tags and billing export. Expect invites for the pilot planning session.
[12:36] [12:40] Jordan: Thanks everyone, appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the docs and the trial link.
[12:45] Evan: Thanks, bye.
[12:47] Marta: Bye.
[12:48] Samir: Thanks.

Note: Transcript has occasional transcription artifacts and imprecise speaker attribution in some lines.
